open_points.subject: A13 confirmation binding digest
open_points.text: “kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order” does not declare the order, serialization, digest algorithm, or treatment of absent and blank values
open_points.question: How are confirmation-bound inputs converted into bytes and digested so showing and submitting the same inputs always compare identically?
options: Declare a canonical ordered encoding and cryptographic digest
Bind and compare structured values directly
Leave the encoding to the implementation
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned canonical encoding with explicit absent-value markers and SHA-256.

open_points.subject: A13 expired confirmation with a different submitted value
open_points.text: “an expired one is refused and cleared” conflicts with “giving another value, is refused and leaves the pending value as it was” when the pending value is expired and the submission gives another value
open_points.question: Does a mismatched submission clear a pending confirmation that has already expired?
options: Clear every expired pending confirmation before comparing the submitted value
Treat value mismatch first and leave the expired confirmation pending
open_points.default_guess: Clear the expired confirmation before comparing values.

open_points.subject: A13 generated-value collision
open_points.text: “The session's identity, its CSRF value and a confirmation value are each at least 32 bytes from the operating system's random source” does not say what happens if a generated owner-session identity duplicates a live identity or another generated value collides where uniqueness matters
open_points.question: Must Registry detect a generated-value collision and retry, or may it overwrite, reuse, or refuse?
options: Detect collisions and generate again
Refuse the operation
Assume collisions cannot occur
open_points.default_guess: Detect collisions in the applicable namespace and generate again.

open_points.subject: A14 confirmation id for an empty audit erasure
open_points.text: A14 rule 5 says “A confirmation id is minted only for an accepted, confirmed action that changes state” and “a confirmed action that changes nothing mints none”, while A15 rule 6 says an erasure removing no entry “still writes its own entry ... with its confirmation id”
open_points.question: Does an accepted audit erasure that removes no old entry mint and record a confirmation id?
options: Yes, make audit erasure an explicit exception to A14 rule 5
No, omit the confirmation id when nothing was removed
open_points.default_guess: Mint and record it, following A15 rule 6 and R0-66.

open_points.subject: A16 validation scope for unpicked records
open_points.text: Rule 1 says the mapping shows “every malformed record and every id that conflicts”, while rule 3 says records only of projects not picked “are neither checked, shown as conflicts nor imported”; the only explicit upload-wide exceptions are an unreadable format and duplicate project records
open_points.question: Which malformed records and conflicts outside the picked projects must be detected or shown?
options: Only unreadable format and duplicate project ids are upload-wide; all other validation is limited to picked projects and their records
Validate and show every malformed record and conflict in the file
Validate all records but show only problems affecting picks
open_points.default_guess: Apply only the two stated upload-wide checks globally and validate all other records only when their project is picked.

open_points.subject: A16 file digest
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest” and “closure.file_digest = digest(f)” do not declare the digest algorithm or whether it covers the exact uploaded bytes or a parsed canonical form
open_points.question: What exact digest identifies an import file in the mapping, confirmation, closure, and audit entry?
options: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with a declared algorithm
Digest a canonical serialization of the parsed file
Let the implementation choose
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: A16 concurrent upload and confirmation in one owner session
open_points.text: “another file is uploaded in that session” replaces the kept file, while confirmation applies the kept file of the bound digest, but the rules do not order a confirmation racing an upload in the same session
open_points.question: If upload and confirmation overlap in one owner session, which file state does confirmation observe and may it commit using the replaced file?
options: Serialize all mutations of one owner session
Let confirmation retain and apply the file it observed before replacement
Let upload invalidate any confirmation still running
open_points.default_guess: Serialize owner-session mutations so one request wholly precedes the other.

open_points.subject: A16 post-import backup on a day already backed up
open_points.text: A16 says “right after it Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule”, while A18 says the import run “counts as that day's backup” and “at most one backup is made per UTC day”
open_points.question: What happens when an import is accepted after a checked daily backup already exists for that UTC day?
options: Make an additional post-import backup despite the daily limit
Replace that day's earlier backup with a new post-import backup
Skip the special run and wait until the next day
open_points.default_guess: Replace the earlier same-day backup with a newly checked post-import backup.

open_points.subject: A17 failed-start side effects
open_points.text: Registry “serves nothing until every check passes”, but rule 5 may create a new empty store and probes the backup location by creating and removing a file; it does not say whether these mutations may remain when a later configuration check fails
open_points.question: Must all non-mutating checks pass before Registry creates a store or probe file, and what state may a failed start leave behind?
options: Perform all possible validation first and clean up every probe; a failed start creates no store
Allow a valid new store to remain after a later check fails
Make startup initialization transactional
open_points.default_guess: Run non-mutating checks first, remove probes, and do not create the store unless all other checks pass.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption and key digest
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” and it records “a digest of the key” without declaring the authenticated-encryption format, nonce handling, algorithm, key interpretation, or digest algorithm
open_points.question: What cryptographic format must every release use to encrypt, authenticate, identify, and later restore a backup?
options: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption format and a separate declared key identifier
Let each release choose and record its format
Use encryption without authenticated metadata
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption format with random nonces and a declared SHA-256 key identifier.

open_points.subject: A18 last backup-run status
open_points.text: “The owner interface shows ... whether the last run failed” does not say where that result is kept or what the interface shows after a restart, although backups themselves record only successful kept runs
open_points.question: Is the last-run result durable across restarts, and how is ‘last run’ determined when the latest attempt produced no kept backup?
options: Persist a non-personal backup-run status record
Keep it only in runtime memory and show unknown after restart
Infer only successful runs from kept backup files
open_points.default_guess: Persist the instant and outcome of the latest attempted run outside the backed-up store.

open_points.subject: A18 temporary-file cleanup
open_points.text: “at every start and every run Registry first removes every temporary file left there” does not define how Registry distinguishes its temporary files from other files in the configured backup location
open_points.question: Exactly which files is Registry authorized to classify and delete as its temporary backup or check files?
options: Use and delete only files matching a reserved, validated Registry naming scheme
Require the backup directory to contain no unrelated files
Delete every filesystem temporary file in the directory
open_points.default_guess: Use a reserved filename prefix plus validated metadata and delete only files Registry created under that scheme.

open_points.subject: A18 backup behavior during restored owner-only operation
open_points.text: A18 says “An owner-only start makes no run” so no backup is made before reconciliation, while R0-89 permits the import to be made again after restoring a pre-import backup and A16 requires a backup run immediately after an accepted import
open_points.question: If the owner repeats the import during the mandatory owner-only recovery phase, does its special post-import backup run, and must reconciliation finish before that import?
options: Require reconciliation first, then permit the import and its special backup even in owner-only mode
Suppress the import backup until service-token mode starts
Refuse import during owner-only recovery
open_points.default_guess: Require reconciliation first and then allow the import's special checked backup in owner-only mode.

open_points.subject: A01 archived project create replay
open_points.text: Rule 3 and required test 4 say a repeat of a project's create after archive answers the archived project, but the formal invariant says “rights fail or project archived => refused” for a create whose request id already exists
open_points.question: Does the archived-project refusal in the formal invariant apply only to room and pointer creates, or also to replaying the project's own create?
options: Limit the archived-parent check to Room and ArtifactPointer creates
Refuse a Project create replay after archive
open_points.default_guess: Limit it to Room and ArtifactPointer creates and allow the archived Project replay.

open_points.subject: A01 server-minted identity collision
open_points.text: Creates and an accepted import mint project, customer, room or pointer identities, but no rule says what happens if the minted UUID is already present in that identity's namespace
open_points.question: On a collision of a Registry-minted identity with an existing record, must Registry retry generation, refuse atomically, or surface an internal failure?
options: Detect the collision and mint again within the transaction
Refuse the action without change
Treat it as an internal error
open_points.default_guess: Detect the collision and mint again before committing.

open_points.subject: A04 simultaneous changes from one revision
open_points.text: “Every action is atomic” and stale revisions are refused, but the text does not state that concurrent read-check-change operations on the same revision are serialized or use a conditional commit
open_points.question: Can two concurrent changing actions that both state the same current revision both be accepted, or must exactly one win and the other be stale?
options: Serialize changes per revised record so only one is accepted
Use an atomic compare-and-change with the same one-winner result
Allow both if each passed its check before either committed
open_points.default_guess: Use atomic compare-and-change so exactly one changing action is accepted and the other is refused as stale.
